description: Authored record-handling fixture, not an agent transcript or a learning result. Never seed this into real personality state.

sections.Observe: The scenario starts with a direct edit to generated bindings in components/demo. Regeneration overwrites it.
sections.Evidence: Authored fixture only; no real agent, generator, or test was run. The hypothetical original diff is overwritten when the local generator is run.
sections.Interpret: A schema-first change may prevent this loss for this generator.
sections.Uncertainty: This scenario illustrates record structure. It is not empirical or causal evidence of learning.

sections.Trigger: An authorized change to generated bindings in components/demo.
sections.Practice: Find the local schema, edit it, regenerate, inspect the output diff, and run the component checks.
sections.Exceptions: Read-only investigation is not authorization to edit or regenerate files. Stop before any side effect not permitted by the current request.
sections.Expected result: The intended change survives regeneration without unrelated losses.
sections.Review plan: Check a later authorized modification and a case where this procedure should not be applied.
sections.Change rationale: Tentative practice extracted from E-example-origin; no established personal trait is claimed.

sections.Observe: A later hypothetical request asks only for a read-only investigation. The agent retrieves L-example-schema@1, reads its boundary, and leaves files unchanged.
sections.Evidence: Authored fixture only; no real agent, generator, or test was run. The scenario records an inspection report and unchanged files, not a regeneration run.
sections.Interpret: The procedure is related but its modifying steps do not fit the current authority.
sections.Uncertainty: This scenario illustrates record structure. It is not empirical or causal evidence of learning.

sections.Situation: Current request: inspect demo schema read-only. Query term schema comes from the request; regeneration is a hint from prior context. Candidate: L-example-schema@1.
sections.Application: Rejected the modifying procedure after checking its read-only exception and the current request. Performed only the authorized inspection.
sections.Outcome: E-example-readonly records unchanged files and an inspection report in this authored scenario. There is no generator execution result.
sections.Assessment: Justified non-application. This checks the decision boundary, not the effectiveness of the schema-first procedure. It must not become supporting evidence.

sections.Observe: A separate hypothetical task authorizes a binding change. The agent checks L-example-schema@1, edits the schema, regenerates, and inspects the diff.
sections.Evidence: Authored fixture only; no real agent, generator, or test was run. The authored scenario states that regeneration retains the intended field and the relevant checks pass; these are not actually executed tests.
sections.Interpret: The scoped practice is consistent with the successful result described by the fixture.
sections.Uncertainty: This scenario illustrates record structure. It is not empirical or causal evidence of learning.

sections.Situation: A new authorized change in components/demo; schema comes from the request. Candidate: L-example-schema@1.
sections.Application: Applied after checking the component, the current request, and allowed writes. Edited the source schema instead of generated output.
sections.Outcome: E-example-applied describes a preserved field and passing checks in the hypothetical scenario.
sections.Assessment: Scoped support in the example, not proof of causation or transfer to other generators. No real model behavior has been evaluated.

sections.Decision: Retain the scoped practice, link the later support, and retain the read-only boundary.
sections.Evidence assessment: V-example-applied supports the scenario practice; V-example-readonly is not effectiveness evidence. Both remain inspectable.
sections.Planned changes: Publish L-example-schema@2 with active status and V-example-applied in support. No instruction-file updates.

sections.Observe: A subsequent hypothetical project change makes an external schema authoritative. Applying the old local-schema-first procedure drops a field when regenerating.
sections.Evidence: Authored fixture only; no real agent, generator, or test was run. The authored output diff loses a required field. This counterexample concerns L-example-schema@2 in changed conditions.

metadata.title: A changed premise challenges the practice

sections.Situation: Generated bindings remain in components/demo, but schema authority has moved. The agent considered L-example-schema@2 applicable without checking that premise.
sections.Application: Applied the old local-schema procedure under an authorized write task; authorization did not make the technical premise correct.
sections.Outcome: E-example-counter describes a dropped required field in the synthetic scenario.
sections.Assessment: Counterexample to the unqualified practice in the changed environment. Contest it and investigate authority before proposing a narrower replacement; do not erase prior support.

sections.Decision: Mark the lesson contested rather than keep applying an unchecked premise.
sections.Evidence assessment: Retain V-example-applied and the original event. V-example-counter changes confidence in the current scope, not the historical facts of those records.
sections.Planned changes: Publish L-example-schema@3 with the counterexample and contested status. Further investigation is pending; no narrower procedure has been validated.
